findings.title: `PasswordField` show/hide password toggle fails when `type="password"` is passed
findings.body: In `PasswordField`, `{...props}` is spread on `InputField` at line 39, after `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` at line 36. Any caller that passes `type="password"` (such as `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` at line 176, which was converted from `TextField` to `PasswordField` in this PR) overwrites the internal `type` prop, making the eye-icon toggle button unable to reveal the password. `type={isPasswordVisible ? "text" : "password"}` should be placed after `{...props}` (or `type` should be omitted from the spread props).

findings.title: Closing the 2FA modal via overlay or Escape on the backup codes step leaves the parent UI out of sync
findings.body: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, 2FA is already enabled on the server once `handleEnable` succeeds and transitions to `SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes` (line 135), but `onEnable()` is now only called when clicking the custom `Close` button (line 269). If the user dismisses the dialog at the backup-codes step by clicking the backdrop, pressing Escape, or clicking the dialog's close icon (`onOpenChange`), `onEnable` is never invoked and `resetState()` is never run. The parent settings page therefore keeps the 2FA switch in the unchecked/disabled state even though 2FA is active on the account, and reopening the modal starts on the backup codes step instead of resetting.

findings.title: Third-party IdP users with 2FA enabled cannot use backup codes or lacks "Lost access" option on login
findings.body: In `next-auth-options.ts` lines 113-129, the checks `if (user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)` and `if (!user.password && user.identityProvider !== IdentityProvider.CAL && !credentials.totpCode)` only bypass password/IdP checks when `credentials.totpCode` is provided, not when `credentials.backupCode` is provided. Additionally, in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` line 180, when `totpEmail` is set (the 2FA flow for Google/SAML users), `ExternalTotpFooter` is rendered instead of `TwoFactorFooter`, which omits the "Lost access" button altogether. As a result, users who authenticate via a third-party identity provider and have 2FA enabled cannot use backup codes to log in.

findings.title: First 2FA E2E test leaves the backup codes modal open and asserts a Promise object is truthy
findings.body: In the first E2E test (`should allow a user to enable 2FA and login using 2FA`), after `fillOtp` on line 44, the modal now transitions to the `DisplayBackupCodes` step rather than closing and calling `onEnable()`. Because the test never clicks `backup-codes-close`, `onEnable()` is never triggered and the switch stays unchecked. As noted in the `FIXME` comment added on line 50, `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy()` only passes because `locator.isChecked()` returns a `Promise<boolean>` (which is always truthy without `await`), not because the switch is actually checked. This test should close the backup codes step (or use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()`) so it actually verifies the post-setup state.
